title: Most people in the Bible who are remembered have famous names.
paragraphs: Most people in the Bible who are remembered have famous names.

David.
Moses.
Paul.
Peter.
But one man helped fulfill prophecy and his name was never recorded.
He owned a donkey.
And one day, two strangers came to untie it.
Imagine the moment.

Early morning in Jerusalem.
The air heavy with the anticipation of Passover.
Pilgrims filling the streets.
Dust rising from the narrow stone roads.
Then two men approach his animal and begin to untie it.
Naturally, he asks the question anyone would ask:
“Why are you untying the colt?”
And they answer with a single sentence that changes the moment forever:

“The Lord has need of it.”
— Luke 19:31
And somehow… that was enough.

No argument.
No contract.
No guarantee it would be returned.
He simply let it go.
That donkey would soon carry Jesus Christ into Jerusalem in what we now call the Triumphal Entry.
Crowds would shout:

“Hosanna!”
“Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!”

Palm branches would wave.
Garments would be thrown on the road.
Prophecy from Zechariah 9:9 would be fulfilled:
“Behold, your King is coming to you; righteous and having salvation, humble and mounted on a donkey.”

And hidden inside that historic moment…
is an unnamed man who simply released what he owned when Jesus asked for it.
That is the lesson.
We often think God only uses the famous, the powerful, or the visible.
But Scripture quietly reminds us of something deeper:
God also builds His purposes through ordinary people who are willing to let go.
Think about it.

The man did not preach a sermon.
He did not perform a miracle.
He did not write Scripture.
But he gave Jesus what he had.
And that was enough to place him inside one of the most important moments in the Gospel story.
Here is the truth many people miss:
The Kingdom of God often moves forward on surrendered ordinary things.

A boy once surrendered five loaves and two fish.
A fisherman surrendered his boat so Jesus could teach from it.
A woman surrendered expensive perfume at Jesus’ feet.
And here, a man surrendered a donkey.
None of those things looked impressive at first.
But when they were placed in Jesus’ hands, they became part of miracles, ministry, and history.
That is still how God works today.
Many people are waiting for something big to give God.

A bigger platform.
More money.
More time.
More influence.
But God often begins with what you already have.

Your home.
Your skills.
Your encouragement.
Your obedience.
Your resources.
Your availability.
The man with the donkey teaches us a powerful truth:
What feels ordinary in your hands can become sacred in God’s purpose.
Another detail is easy to miss.
The owner released the donkey before he saw the crowd.

Before the palm branches.
Before the celebration.
Before the prophecy unfolding.
He obeyed without seeing the full outcome.
That is what real faith looks like.
Sometimes God does not show you the entire story first.
Sometimes all you hear is:
“The Lord has need of it.”
And you must decide whether that is enough.
This moment also confronts something in the human heart.
We like control.

We like ownership.
Security.
Plans.
But discipleship often requires surrender.
Sometimes the very thing we hold tightly is the very thing God wants to place into His mission.
Imagine if that man had refused.
Imagine if he had said:

“That donkey is too valuable.”
“What if I need it later?”
“What if it never comes back?”
But instead, he loosened the rope.
And because he did, that donkey carried the King.
Read that again.
Because he loosened the rope, his ordinary possession carried the King of Kings.
That is the power of surrender.
God does not ask everyone to stand on the stage.
But He does ask everyone to open their hands.

Some people will preach.
Some will lead.
Some will travel.
Some will teach.
But others will quietly provide the donkey.
And heaven sees all of it.
Jesus once said something that reveals how God views these acts:

“Whoever gives even a cup of cold water… will by no means lose his reward.”
— Matthew 10:42
In God's Kingdom, faithfulness is never small.
The world celebrates fame.
But heaven celebrates obedience.
The unnamed man reminds us of something beautiful:
You do not have to be famous to be faithful.

You do not have to be seen to matter.
You do not have to lead the parade to be part of the purpose.
Sometimes your role is simply to release what God asks for.
And when you do, something incredible happens.
Your ordinary life becomes connected to God's extraordinary story.
So maybe the real question today is this:
What donkey in your life is still tied up?

Is it your time?
Your talent?
Your resources?
Your influence?
Your calling?
Your obedience?
What is God asking you to untie?
Because the truth is simple:
Anything surrendered to Jesus can carry glory.
And somewhere in heaven’s record…

There is still room for unnamed people
who simply loosen the rope when the Lord asks.
Reflection Question for Engagement
What is one “ordinary” thing in your life that you believe God might be asking you to surrender for His purpose?
